headline: Reach the end using at least two dictionary pieces
statement: Given distinct nonempty dictionary words, return all words that can be formed by concatenating at least two shorter dictionary words. A component word may be reused.
constraints: Words contain lowercase English letters and are unique
intuition: For each word, try splitting it into shorter dictionary words. Save which character boundaries can be reached by valid pieces. Reaching the end proves a split exists, but the original word alone must not count. Skip the transition that uses the entire candidate as one piece.
approach: Store all words in a set.
For each candidate, initialize reachable boundary 0.
At every end boundary, try reachable starts and dictionary substrings, skipping the whole-word segment.
Accept if the final boundary is reachable.
correctness: reachable[end] becomes true exactly when the prefix through end can be split into dictionary entries: a transition extends a previously valid prefix with one entry. Excluding start=0,end=len(word) removes the only one-piece decomposition, so an accepted whole word necessarily uses at least two shorter entries.
bruteForce: Try every cut pattern within each word: O(2^L) segmentations.

complexity.explanation: For a word of length L, O(L²) boundary pairs may be considered. Python creates a substring copy and hashes its characters, each taking O(segment length), so the conservative bound is O(L³) per word. The dictionary and O(max L) reachability table determine working storage; output is excluded.

pitfalls: The word itself must not count as its only component.
Repeated use of a shorter word is allowed.
A concatenated word can also be a component of a longer one.
